cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses again. No feast this time, no calendar, just the lamps. And lamps don't run on good vibes, friend. They need oil.

cards.question: Who does the LORD tell Moses to command to bring the oil for the lamps?
The lamp oil isn't just any oil. It's to be pure oil of pressed ___, brought for the light.
The LORD wants that pure olive oil brought for the light. What is it meant to do?

answers.text: Light the lamps on feast days
Fill the lamps once a year

cards.text: Now the LORD names the man on lamp duty: Aaron, Moses' brother and Israel's high priest. His spot is in the Tent of Meeting, just outside the veil of the Testimony.

cards.question: Aaron is to tend the lamps before the LORD continually, from ___ until morning.
Tending these lamps is a job meant to end once Aaron's generation is gone.
Aaron keeps those lamps burning before the LORD. What do the lamps sit on?

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses a second job, and friend, it's BAKING. Fine flour, two-tenths of an ephah per loaf, and I have NEVER felt more seen by a chapter of Leviticus.

cards.question: Moses is to bake loaves from fine flour for the LORD. How many loaves?
The twelve loaves go on the table of pure gold before the LORD, set in ___ rows with ___ loaves per row.
The loaves sit in their rows on the gold table. What does the LORD say to place near each row?

cards.text: That frankincense serves as a memorial portion for the bread, a food offering to the LORD. It is NOT a topping, friend, so put the sprinkles down.

cards.question: The bread is set out before the LORD just once a year, at the Feast of Tabernacles.
Every Sabbath day, the bread is set out before the LORD on behalf of the ___ as a permanent covenant.

cards.text: Fresh loaves every Sabbath. Which brings up the question every baker asks the second a batch comes out: who gets to eat it?

cards.question: The bread set out before the LORD belongs to someone. Who eats it?
Aaron and his sons can eat this bread anywhere they like, even back in their own tents.

cards.text: To Aaron, it's a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD, his portion forever. That's where we'll stop for now, friend, but the LORD isn't done teaching His people about being holy.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'The LORD speaks to Moses again.' / 'No feast this time, no calendar, just the lamps.' / 'And lamps don't run on good vibes, friend.' / 'They need oil.' The opening card can have no more than 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: 'No feast this time, no calendar' is a callback to Leviticus 23, the previous passage. It is provided for context only and isn't part of this lesson, so nothing in this lesson sets the callback up.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: 'just the lamps' says the LORD's speech is only about the lamps. The same speech goes on to give the instructions for the twelve loaves (Lev 24:5-9), so the text shows this line is untrue.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: On card 1, 'No feast this time' points the baker away from the wrong answer 'Light the lamps on feast days' on card 4. It also leans against 'at the Feast of Tabernacles' in the card 14 statement.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the priests', 'Only the elders') and the right answer doesn't. That makes the wrong answers read as a pair and the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: 'Aaron, Moses' brother and Israel's high priest' uses facts from outside the passage (for example Exodus 4:14 and Leviticus 21:10). The card cites only Leviticus 24:3 and gives no reference for them.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question asks what the lamps sit on. The right answer, 'The pure gold lampstand', is the only option with 'lamp' in it, so a baker can match the word instead of reasoning it out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card tells 'Fresh loaves every Sabbath', which is from Leviticus 24:8, but it cites only Leviticus 24:9. It only sets up the question from verse 9 and doesn't tell anything from it. The citation should start at Leviticus 24:8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
